title: Oxymoron examples: how can silence be deafening?
practice: Look for another unexpected link between words in Connections.

sections.html:
An oxymoron combines apparently contradictory words or ideas in one expression. “Deafening silence” is an example: deafening suggests overwhelming noise, while silence suggests its absence. Oxford’s dictionary uses this very phrase.

Imagine telling a joke at dinner. You finish. Nobody laughs. Someone quietly reaches for the potatoes. The silence might feel enormous, even though it makes no sound. Calling it deafening captures that awkward feeling better than merely calling the room quiet.
sections.title: A silence that makes itself heard

sections.html:
Bittersweet holds two opposing feelings inside one word. Picture a friend leaving for an exciting adventure: you are pleased for them and sad to say goodbye. One word leaves room for both.

Cruel kindness puts a harsher idea beside a gentler one. In an imagined story, a friend’s honest criticism might sting while helping someone improve. The context explains the tension. Merriam-Webster includes both examples. Neither expression asks you to throw away one half of the meaning.
sections.title: Two more small contradictions

sections.html:
No. In an earlier lesson about words such as dust, the same word has different meanings in different uses. You choose the intended meaning from the sentence.

With an oxymoron, the opposing ideas appear together. “Deafening silence” keeps the quiet and the sense of overwhelming impact in the same expression. The apparent contradiction is doing useful work; it is not automatically a mistake.
sections.title: Is this the same as a word meaning its opposite?

sections.html:
The name has a pleasing little twist. Merriam-Webster traces its Greek ingredients to meanings of sharp or keen and foolish. The word’s own roots pull in different directions.

When you spot possible oxymoron examples, ask two questions: “Which ideas seem to clash?” and “What does putting them together add?” A plain “quiet room” does not contain that clash. A “deafening silence” gives the room a rather more uncomfortable personality.
